lessons: Use direct second-person 'Imagine you are...' roleplay hooks (e.g. 'सोचो, तुम...') to maximize initial 10% retention (up to 1.055).
Avoid dumping heavy scientific stats and technical numbers (e.g., '34,500 newton', detailed anatomy) too early; Video 2 lost 23% at once during dense technical specs.
Frame science concepts around relatable everyday comparisons (e.g., comparing T. rex weight to 6 cars) to maintain strong 50% retention (49.17% in Video 1).
Keep hooks concise and scenario-driven rather than trying to explain the core law/mechanism immediately; Video 3 had a 19.1% early drop due to a dense, explanatory hook.
worst_moment_types: Dense technical measurements and jargon-heavy scientific lists (e.g. Newton forces, jaw specs).
Overly explanatory initial hook lines that try to summarize the whole concept upfront instead of building curiosity.
best_hook_types: Second-person roleplay/hypothetical scenarios ('Imagine you are... / सोचो, तुम...')
Myth-busting question hooks that challenge popular media tropes (e.g., standing still in front of a T. rex).
